feedback: Based only on iteration 0, which ran off track on all 60 trials with progress 0.04 to 0.115, one line-loss event per track, and low steering_oscillation (0.065 to 0.073). The low jitter suggests the 0.04 m lookahead is not oscillating, so the main problem is early drift off the line, not damping. Your 40 mm span produced one line-loss event on every track, which is the signal to widen the span; I have adopted x = ±0.025 m. I cannot say yet how this geometry performs. Next race: if line_loss_events is still at least 1 with the 50 mm span, the sensors are not the bottleneck and I will ask you to move the array forward (y 0.05 to 0.06 m) for more reaction time. If line_loss_events is 0 but the robot still leaves the track, the limit is turning authority, so consider mass 0.5 kg for less yaw inertia. Keep the 0.12 m body width unless the off-track limit becomes the binding constraint, because 0.18 m only moves the limit from 0.06 m to about 0.0575 m.
requested_changes: Keep sensor span at x = ±0.025 m (50 mm) with five sensors and the 12 mm footprint, since iteration 0 showed one line-loss event per track at 40 mm.
If line_loss_events is still at least 1 at 50 mm, move the array forward from y = 0.04 m to about 0.05 to 0.06 m, keeping the span unchanged.

If line_loss_events is 0 but the robot still goes off track, reduce mass from 0.6 kg to about 0.5 kg to improve turning response, and report completion_time for any finished run so base_speed can be judged.
